service.description: Internal machine-to-machine callers with no WhatsApp identity behind them - cron_trigger firing a scheduled job, one agent calling another as part of composing a reply. Deliberately not '*': scoped to exactly what today's internal flows need.

adiyan_reader_service.description: AdiyanReader's own outbound calls (mesh/adiyan_reader/skills/start_reading.py, read_next_page.py, dispatch_questions.py) - fetching the next page to narrate, registering the next night's/next morning's one-shot cron_trigger fires, and delivering the nightly reading (text + voice note) plus next-day quiz to whichever phone number that reading job is registered against. mcp.whatsapp.resolve_chat_id/send_message/send_voice replace what used to be a direct, ungated OpenWAService call - see the Developer Guide's pitfall section for why that was a real gap, not a style choice. Its own tier, not 'service': memory.get_book_page has no caller outside AdiyanReader, so there's no reason for it to sit in the shared tier scheduler/journal/etc. also mint tokens against - narrower blast radius if this agent's token is ever misused, same reasoning as config_server_otp above. mcp.cron_trigger.register_trigger stays in 'service' too, since scheduler needs that one as well.

scheduler_service.description: Scheduler's own outbound calls from mesh/scheduler/skills/run_routine.py - crafting a reflection prompt via Journal Agent, and sending the composed reminder to the owner's own WhatsApp. Deliberately its own tier, not 'service': journal.craft_reflection_prompt has no caller outside Scheduler, so it doesn't belong in the shared tier other agents also mint tokens against. mcp.whatsapp.get_own_phone/send_message are a DELIBERATE, conscious re-grant here - the 2026-08-30 lockdown removed WhatsApp send from 'service' specifically to stop Scheduler's automated sends after a runaway-message incident whose root cause (something in penwa, not this codebase) was never fully isolated. Re-added here, scoped to Scheduler alone via AdiyanAgent (mesh/lib/agent_sdk.py) rather than the raw OpenWAService bypass run_routine.py used before, which sent regardless of what this file said. If the incident's root cause resurfaces, remove this tier's WhatsApp keys, not 'service's - 'service' never had them back in the first place.

orchestrator_delivery.description: Orchestrator's own reply-delivery action (mesh/orchestrator/skills/handle_message.py's delivery_token) - sending whatever reply/image/document was already composed, back to whoever's chat triggered this run. Deliberately its own tier, not 'service': confirmed live on 2026-09-01 that reusing 'service' here silently broke EVERY reply Orchestrator ever sends, including a reply to the owner's own self-chat, from the moment the 2026-08-30 lockdown removed WhatsApp send from 'service' - this action was never actually automated/timer-driven the way Scheduler's sends were, it only ever fires once per inbound message already received and processed, so it was never the risk the lockdown was written for. Scoped to exactly the three send tools handle_message.py's delivery step calls - not get_own_phone (that stays on the separate 'service' token minted for is_owner() checks) and not memory.remember_interaction (a separate token, separate purpose, in the same file).

config_server_otp.description: config_server's own OTP-login flow (mesh/config_server/otp.py) sending a dashboard login code to the owner's own WhatsApp. Deliberately its own tier, not 'service': one message per human-initiated login attempt, not an automated/recurring job, so it shouldn't be reopened or closed by whatever policy scheduler/journal's automated sends need.

compute_share_client.description: The AdiyanAgent SDK's own internal identity (mesh/lib/agent_sdk.py's ask()) when it falls back to offloading a prompt to a peer's spare compute - never minted by, or visible to, whichever agent actually called agent.ask(). Deliberately its own platform-level tier rather than something added to every agent's own tier: offloading is a platform capability every agent gets by construction, not something each agent author has to know exists or request access to. Scoped to exactly compute_share.offload - nothing about routing an agent's LLM call needs any other permission.

standard.description: Default tier for a newly registered client - everything a client could already do before permission checks existed.
